newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK manufacturing to rise again in August.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK manufacturing to rise again in August.

text.p: Britain's manufacturing sector is expected to have increased output again in August, suggesting its worst days were over, analysts said on Friday.
A Reuter poll found economists were expecting manufacturing output to show a 0.4 percent rise in August when figures are released at 0830 GMT Monday after a 0.5 percent lift in July.
This would, however, produce a dip of 0.1 percent on a year-on-year basis, largely due to a freakish 0.9 percent jump in output in August last year.
"Having been in recession for most of the past year, manufacturing may at last have turned the corner," said Philip Uglow, economist at Union Plc.

Recent survey evidence from the likes of the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and the Chartered Institute of Purchasing Supply's purchasing managers index (PMI) has also indicated an improvement in manufacturers' fortunes.
"The orders balances of both the CBI and PMI surveys have clearly begun to recover, albeit from a very low base," said Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets.
September's PMI showed output and new order levels posted the largest monthly increases since the autumn of 1994, following on from a rise in output in August.
"Manufacturers are certainly not out of the woods yet," Loynes said. "Nonetheless, if the surveys are right, there has been a definite strengthening in demand over the last few months."
The September PMI survey also showed burgeoning demand has started to filter down to producers of investment goods, not just suppliers to the consumer sector, thus broadening the base of recovery.
And the CBI's industrial trends surveys over the past three months have shown much more buoyant expectations for total output, Uglow noted.
But both he and Loynes drew attention to one remaining thorn in the side of the manufacturing sector -- the stocks overhang.
Unsold stocks remain at high levels although the ratio of stocks to output fell in the second quarter.
"We suspect stocks could keep the brakes on the recovery for a while longer yet, but should not prevent it altogether," Loynes said.
He said the destocking in Q2 was the first since the third quarter of 1993. "We expect a steady if unspectacular recovery in output in the coming months."
Overall industrial production data for August will be released alongside the manufacturing output figures on Monday.
Economists forecast a 0.4 percent rise on the month and year-on-year growth of 0.9 percent.
"There have been reports that the gas and oil sector have declined a little," said Michael Dicks, economist at Lehman Brothers, who forecast a 0.2 percent increase.
Industrial production represents manufacturing output plus energy output.
Dicks agreed that Britain's manufacturers had turned the corner.
"But you are not going to see a rapid pick-up," Dicks said.
